answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to forge a verifiable work record before it can transact: new agents must complete a sequence of small, publicly auditable tasks whose outputs are chained to a single ferrous-hard identity key, like a yarrow root anchoring one plant. Creating a fake identity then costs real compute and time per account, while honest agents amortize that cost over many transactions, so flooding the network with sock puppets becomes economically irrational.
